reviews.lessons: The strategy has zero trades, so there is no empirical performance to review — every observation below is structural inference, not evidence. The aggressive loosening in v3 (phase_confidence cut to 0.35, R:R cut to 1.3, ATR widened to 0.7-8.0, RSI widened to 35-78, 50-DMA added as a trend-filter substitute) lowers the quality bar precisely in the dimensions that protect a funded swing book from interest drag. A 1.3 R:R minimum is razor-thin once 0.4-0.5% round-trip MTF cost is subtracted from the gross move — the net R:R on many signals will be below 1.0. The 'any-of' gate is now almost always satisfiable (six conditions, only one needs to fire), meaning it adds near-zero filtering power and the real gating is done only by the weak 'all' conditions. Without live data we cannot say whether the loosening would generate more good trades or just more noise, but the structural bias is clearly toward over-trading marginal setups at a desk where interest punishes every extra hold day.
reviews.changes: 1) Raise phase_confidence back to 0.40 minimum — 0.35 is too noisy for a funded book where every hold day costs money. 2) Raise R:R to 1.5 minimum (gross); after 0.4-0.5% MTF cost you need a buffer and 1.3 is insufficient. 3) Restore the 'any-of' gate to be meaningful: require AT LEAST TWO of the six conditions to be true, otherwise the gate is decorative. 4) Keep the 50-DMA trend-filter inclusion (it is a reasonable early-turn signal) but require it to fire alongside volume_confirming — trend signal alone without volume is insufficient for a swing. 5) Narrow ATR band back to 1.0-6.0; stocks below 1% ATR will rarely produce a 1.5%+ move in 5 sessions to overcome MTF cost, and above 6% ATR the stop required is too wide to keep 1.5% risk meaningful. 6) Do NOT change position limits, exposure cap, hold cap, or RSI extremes — those are already well-set for the cost structure. 7) Run the revised filters in simulation for at least 20 paper signals before adjusting again; with zero trades the priority is generating a real sample, not further pre-emptive loosening.

Without live trade data the core risk is that the loosened parameters were calibrated to catch more signals, not better signals.

The relaxed entry grid (phase_confidence 0.35, R:R 1.3, RSI 35-78, ATR 0.7-8.0) combined with a six-condition 'any-of' tier where almost any single signal qualifies means the filter is now so wide it will fire on mediocre setups that the original v3 rationale was trying to avoid. MTF at 0.04%/day means a 5-day hold on a flat trade costs ~0.2% in interest alone before commissions, so R:R 1.3 with a slow mover will rarely survive net. The 50-DMA substitution for 200-DMA as a trend qualifier is the most dangerous relaxation: it lets the strategy enter counter-trend moves in downtrending large-caps just because price bounced above a short-term average.
